article_blocks.text: Strain Type: Indica-leaning hybrid
Genetics: Dark Karma × Zabuza
Breeder: Fig Farms
THC Content: 27%
CBD Content: Generally very low
Terpene Profile: N/A
Primary Flavors: Grape, pineapple, sweet lemon
Flowering Time (Indoor): 9 weeks
Outdoor Harvest Time: October
Indoor Yield: Moderate
Outdoor Yield: Moderate
Grow Difficulty: Moderate to advanced

Fabulosa is the sort of cannabis that refuses to settle into one familiar flavor category. The first impression can resemble dark grape medicine, but the sweetness quickly shifts toward sticky pineapple juice before an unexpectedly savory combination of cheese, pine, earth, and diesel begins to emerge. Fig Farms bred the strain by putting its Dark Karma female together with a selected male from Umami Seed Co.’s Zabuza, then hunting the resulting offspring for the expression it wanted to preserve. The flower is visually striking, yet appearance is only part of its appeal. Its unusual strength is balance: a modern, resin-heavy weed capable of producing strong euphoria and sensory enhancement without automatically turning into the kind of heavy indica that ends the evening early.
Genetics and Lineage

The direct pedigree is Dark Karma × Zabuza. Fig Farms bred and selected the cultivar in-house, using a Zabuza male from Umami Seed Co. that stood out for its blocky flower structure and dramatic color expression. The female side comes from Dark Karma, another Fig Farms creation. Fig Farms lists Dark Karma as Dutch Treat × Strange Love, while High Times further identifies Strange Love as a Goji OG × Snow Lotus line from Bodhi Seeds . That gives Fabulosa a much broader genetic foundation than the two-parent name initially suggests, bringing together Dutch Treat, Bodhi-derived genetics, and contemporary Umami breeding.

Zabuza supplies an equally modern side of the family. High Times identifies that parent as Poison Gushers × Zuchi, and Fig Farms specifically emphasizes the male’s contribution to structure and color. The pairing therefore combines a female already valued for unusual flavor and visual expression with a male selected for architecture and appearance. Rather than simply chasing higher THC or stacking fashionable names, the cross reflects Fig Farms’ broader breeding philosophy of searching for sensory qualities that do not resemble the rest of the market.
Effects and Experience

Fabulosa’s effect profile is unusually useful for a strain with an indica-leaning reputation. The beginning tends to be cerebral and positive, with mood elevation arriving before substantial physical heaviness. Conversation may feel easier, music becomes more immersive, and routine activities can acquire a slightly brighter quality. Rather than producing a narrow burst of stimulation, the experience often feels open and comfortable, making the weed adaptable to social settings, creative downtime, a meal, or an evening spent watching a movie.

What separates the cultivar from many heavy modern hybrids is what does not happen next. High Times specifically noted that Fabulosa did not become a knockout strain and described it as suitable alongside either daytime or nighttime activities. Physical relaxation can develop, but it does not necessarily erase mental engagement or push the consumer immediately toward sleep. That makes the effect feel more balanced than the visual density and rich aroma might suggest.

Potency can still be considerable, and the smooth experience should not be mistaken for mild cannabis. Large servings may produce stronger body weight, impaired short-term memory, dry mouth, dry eyes, dizziness, or anxiety in THC-sensitive consumers. As with any high-potency marijuana, the chemistry of the actual batch matters more than a generalized strain reputation.
Medical Benefits

Some medical marijuana consumers may find the combination of mental uplift and moderate physical relaxation preferable to a strongly sedating cultivar. The euphoric portion of the experience may temporarily reduce the prominence of everyday stress or low mood, while the calmer physical component can make it easier to unwind without necessarily eliminating functionality.

THC-containing cannabis is also used by some patients for appetite loss, nausea, discomfort, and sleep-related concerns. Fabulosa may overlap with those broader effects depending on dose and individual response, but the strain itself has not been evaluated in controlled clinical research for any specific condition.

For medical use, batch-specific laboratory information is more meaningful than the weed strain name . Cannabinoid concentration, terpene composition, tolerance, medications, and personal physiology all affect how marijuana is experienced. Anyone using cannabis therapeutically alongside prescription drugs or for a significant health condition should discuss it with an appropriate healthcare professional.
Flavor Profile and Aroma

Flavor is where Fabulosa becomes particularly distinctive. Fig Farms describes the aroma in unusually specific terms: grape medicine, sticky pineapple juice, and skunky cheese. Those three impressions occupy very different sensory territory, yet they fit together in the finished flower. Sweet dark fruit and tropical juice create the opening, while a savory fermented quality appears underneath and prevents the profile from becoming another straightforward fruit-candy hybrid.

Other Fig Farms product descriptions emphasize sweet lemon, woody pine, and savory diesel, revealing another side of the same genetic expression. Pine and fuel give the flower a drier, more traditional marijuana character beneath the tropical sweetness. Earth and spice may become more apparent on the exhale, especially after the brighter fruit notes recede.

No universal compound-level terpene panel has been published by Fig Farms for Fabulosa, so assigning an exact dominant terpene would create more certainty than the breeder data supports. Its aromatic identity is better described from the breeder’s sensory record: grape, pineapple, citrus, pine, cheese, and diesel interacting in a profile that is both fruity and distinctly savory.
Growing Information

Fig Farms has released more information about the genetic selection than about home cultivation. The company does not currently publish an official flowering duration, plant height, indoor yield, outdoor harvest window, or feeding recommendation for Fabulosa. Those unknowns should remain explicit rather than being replaced with generic eight-to-nine-week estimates borrowed from unrelated hybrids.

What Fig Farms does document is the importance of its Zabuza male. The breeder selected that plant partly for its blocky structure and striking colorway, and those traits carry into the finished Fabulosa flowers. Mature buds are notably dense and resin-heavy, giving the cultivar the polished appearance associated with Fig Farms’ contemporary indoor breeding program.

Dense flowers create practical considerations regardless of the precise cultivation schedule. Strong airflow and disciplined humidity control become increasingly important late in bloom because compact cannabis flowers can retain moisture internally. Until Fig Farms publishes a full grow specification or releases the genetics more broadly, precise yield and harvest claims should be treated cautiously.
FAQ
What are the genetics of Fabulosa?

Fabulosa is Dark Karma × Zabuza. Fig Farms bred and pheno-hunted the strain itself. Dark Karma is listed by Fig Farms as Dutch Treat × Strange Love, while Zabuza contributes Poison Gushers and Zuchi genetics.
Who bred the Fabulosa strain?
Fig Farms bred Fabulosa and selected the keeper phenotype. The company used an in-house Dark Karma female with a selected male from Umami Seed Co.’s Zabuza line.
Is Fabulosa indica or sativa?

It is best described as an indica-leaning hybrid. Its effects are more balanced than a traditional heavy indica, however, with noticeable euphoria and mental engagement occurring without pronounced sedation at moderate doses.
What does Fabulosa taste like?

The breeder describes grape medicine, pineapple juice, and skunky cheese, while other Fig Farms descriptions add sweet lemon, woody pine, earth, and savory diesel. The combination creates a funky fruit profile with a distinctly savory finish.
How long does Fabulosa take to flower?

Fig Farms has not publicly released an official flowering time for Fabulosa. Exact flowering schedules published by unaffiliated strain databases or seed sellers should therefore not be treated as confirmed specifications for the authentic Fig Farms cultivar.
Final Thoughts on Fabulosa

Fabulosa illustrates why Fig Farms has built a reputation around unusual in-house breeding rather than simply reproducing whatever genetic families are currently fashionable. Dark Karma brings established Fig Farms character into the cross, while the selected Zabuza male contributes structure, color, and another layer of contemporary genetics. The outcome is marijuana with an aroma that moves unpredictably from grape and pineapple to cheese, pine, citrus, earth, and diesel.

Its effect profile may be even more important than the flavor. Strong euphoria and sociability arrive without automatically giving way to overwhelming sedation, allowing the cultivar to occupy a useful middle ground between daytime flower and heavy nighttime weed. Combined with dense trichome-rich buds and a terpene profile unlike the standard candy-gas formula, Fabulosa is one of Fig Farms’ more distinctive recent creations and a notable example of where modern California cannabis breeding is moving.
